The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[4–7] ﴿Or do those who commit evil deeds think that they will outstrip Us? Evil is what they judge.﴾ ﴿Whoever hopes for the meeting with Allah – then indeed the term of Allah is coming, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 5] ﴿And whoever strives, he strives only for himself. That is, let him not be impatient for it, for it is coming by the promise of Allah, the true, and the word of truth. I have not seen anyone mention this, and perhaps it is more fitting given the indication of the context and the preceding passage. The commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on Surah 29, verses 8–9:

On the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[8–9] ﴿And We have enjoined upon man kindness to his parents. But if they strive with you to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, then do not obey them. To Me is your return, and I will inform you of what you used to do.﴾ ﴿And those who believe and do righteous deeds – We will surely admit them among the righteous.﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 9]

﴿And We have enjoined upon man kindness to his parents﴾ means: We commanded him with an emphatic command to render to his parents an act of great goodness. ﴿But if they strive with you to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, then do not obey them﴾ means: in associating partners with Me, if they urge you to it. The meaning of ﴿that of which you have no knowledge﴾ is: you have no knowledge of its divinity. Al-Qadi (al-Baydawi) said: He expressed its negation as the negation of knowledge of it, to indicate that what has not been known to be sound may not be followed, even if its falsehood is not known. So how about that whose falsehood is known? ﴿To Me is your return, and I will inform you of what you used to do﴾ means: to Me is the return of everyone among you, whether believer or polytheist, and I will recompense you with your full recompense. In this is a warning against following them in associating partners with God [p. 4739], and an exhortation to steadfastness and uprightness in the religion, by mention of the return and the threat.

It has been related that Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas al-Zuhri, may Allah be pleased with him, when he embraced Islam, his mother said: "O Sa'd! It has reached me that you have turned away (sabi'ta) from your religion. By Allah, the roof of no house shall shade me from the sun's heat (ḍiḥḥ) and the wind, and food and drink are forbidden to me until you disbelieve in Muhammad." She was the dearest of her sons to her. Sa'd refused, and she remained like that for three days. Then Sa'd came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and complained to him, and this verse was revealed, along with the one in Luqman and the one in al-Ahqaf. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ then commanded him to deal gently with her and to win her consent with kindness.

On the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[10] ﴿And among the people is he who says, "We believe in Allah," but when he is harmed for (the sake of) Allah, he regards the trial from people as like the punishment of Allah. ﴿And among the people is he who says, "We believe in Allah," but when he is harmed for (the sake of) Allah, he regards the trial from people as like the punishment of Allah﴾ That is: he makes the various kinds of harm that befall him, because of his turning away from faith, equal in severity and terror to the punishment of Allah, so he apostatizes from the religion. Yet the requirement of his faith is that he should be patient, steadfast, and receive with contentment what he suffers for Allah's sake, seeing the punishment in it as sweetness and the ordeal as a gift. For the final outcome belongs to the God-fearing, and the happiness of both abodes is for its people. ﴿And if victory comes from your Lord, they will surely say, "Indeed, we were with you." The discussion of the words of the Exalted:

[11–13] "And Allah will surely make evident those who believe, and He will surely make evident the hypocrites." (p-4741) "And those who disbelieved said to those who believed, 'Follow our way, and we will bear your sins,' but they will not bear anything of their sins. Indeed, they are liars." [Al-'Ankabut: 12] "And they will surely bear their own burdens and additional burdens along with their burdens. And they will surely be questioned on the Day of Resurrection about what they used to fabricate." [Al-'Ankabut: 13]

"And Allah will surely make evident those who believe" — that is, by their sincerity. "And He will surely make evident the hypocrites." Then the Exalted explained how the disbelievers of Quraysh caused those who believed to return to disbelief through enticement, after having explained how they caused them to do so through harm, by His saying: "And those who disbelieved said to those who believed, 'Follow our way, and we will bear your sins'" [Al-'Ankabut: 12] — that is, if that is a sin for which one is held accountable by resurrection, then let its consequence fall upon us and on our necks.

Indeed, they are liars" [Al-'Ankabut: 12]. He means the burdens of misguiding, of causing others to disbelieve, and of barring from the way of Allah. **(p-4742)** The discussion on the interpretation (*ta'wil*) of His saying, exalted is He:

[14–19] ﴿And We certainly sent Noah to his people, and he remained among them a thousand years less fifty years, and the flood seized them while they were wrongdoers.﴾ ﴿So We saved him and the companions of the ship, and We made it a sign for the worlds.﴾ [Al-Ankabut: 15] ﴿And Abraham, when he said to his people, "Worship Allah and fear Him. That is better for you, if you only knew."﴾ [Al-Ankabut: 16] ﴿You only worship, besides Allah, idols, and you invent a falsehood. Indeed, those you worship besides Allah do not possess for you any provision. So seek provision from Allah, worship Him, and be grateful to Him. To Him you will be returned.﴾ [Al-Ankabut: 17] ﴿And if you deny, then nations before you have denied. ﴿And We certainly sent Noah to his people, and he remained among them a thousand years less fifty years, and the flood seized them while they were wrongdoers.﴾ ﴿So We saved him and the companions of the ship, and We made it a sign﴾ [Al-Ankabut: 15]. That is: this awesome event is an admonition ﴿for the worlds﴾ [Al-Ankabut: 15]. ﴿And Abraham, when he said to his people, "Worship Allah and fear Him. That is better for you, if you only knew."﴾ [Al-Ankabut: 16] ﴿You only worship, besides Allah, idols, and you invent a falsehood﴾ [Al-Ankabut: 17]. That is: a lie, in calling them gods, partners of Allah, and intercessors with Him. ﴿Indeed, those you worship besides Allah do not possess for you any provision. So seek provision from Allah, worship Him, and be grateful to Him. To Him you will be returned.﴾ [Al-Ankabut: 17] ﴿And if (p-4743) you deny, then nations before you have denied. This is through what they witness in themselves of Allah's creation of them after they were not a thing mentioned, then they came into being and became people who hear and see. He who originated this is capable of repeating it. It is easy for Him and effortless for Him. The repetition is by His creating it, exalted is He, every year, like what He created in the previous year of plants, fruits and others. Indeed, that is among what is used as evidence for the validity of resurrection, and its occurrence is without doubt. Then the conjunction is valid.

He said: With this explanation, what was said falls away: if "seeing" is meant as knowledge, then both are known; and if it is meant as sight, then both are not visible. Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 29, verses 20–24:

The discussion of the interpretation of His words, may He be exalted:

[20–24] ﴿Say: "Travel in the earth and observe how He originated creation; then Allah will bring forth the final creation. ﴿Say: "Travel in the earth and observe how He originated creation"﴾, meaning: how He created them at the beginning, in varying stages, differing natures, and diverse characters. [25–29] ﴿And he said: "You have only taken idols besides God out of affection between you in the life of this world; then on the Day of Resurrection some of you will disavow others, and some of you will curse others. ﴿And he said: "You have only taken idols besides God out of affection between you in the life of this world"﴾: that is, so that you may show affection to one another and keep bonds with one another, through your gathering upon their worship. ﴿Then on the Day of Resurrection some of you will disavow others, and some of you will curse others﴾: that is, you will deny what existed between you, and the followers will curse those they followed, and those they followed will curse the followers. [p-4746] NOTE:

Al-Samin (al-Samin al-Halabi) said: Regarding the ﻣﺎ (ma) in His saying ﴿إنما اتخذتم﴾ (innama attakhadhtum) there are three aspects:

The first: it is a relative pronoun (mawsula) meaning "the one who", and its returning pronoun is omitted, which is the first object, and ﴿أوثانا﴾ (awthanan, "idols") is the second object. The discussion of the interpretation of His words, Exalted is He:

[41–44] ﴿The parable of those who take protectors other than Allah is like the spider's, which takes a house; and indeed the weakest of houses is the spider's house, if only they knew.﴾ ﴿Indeed Allah knows what they invoke besides Him of anything; and He is the Mighty, the Wise.﴾ [al-ʿAnkabut: 42] ﴿And these parables We present to the people, but none understands them except the learned.﴾ [al-ʿAnkabut: 43] ﴿Allah created the heavens and the earth in truth. Then, the purpose of the comparison is to establish the feebleness of their religion and that it has reached its extreme in this respect. It is either a compound simile (tashbīh murakkab, a simile drawn from a composite image), in which the pivot of the parable rests on the idea that their protectors are like the spider's web in weakness of state and unfitness to be relied upon. On this view, His words ﴿And indeed the weakest of houses﴾ form a concluding addition (tadhyīl, an appended statement) that clarifies the purpose of the comparison. And His words ﴿if only they knew﴾ are an intensification (īghāl, pressing a point to its furthest extent) in declaring their ignorance, because they do not know it even though it is clear to anyone with the slightest discernment.

Or it may be a simile of the single element (tashbīh al-mufrad), since the aim is to explain the state of the worshipper and the worshipped. The verse contains rhetorical subtleties (laṭāʾif bayāniyya) that are mentioned in the extended works.

As for His words ﴿Indeed Allah knows what they invoke besides Him of anything﴾ [al-ʿAnkabut: 42]: with the yāʾ and the tāʾ in (tadʿūna) there are two readings. The word (ma) is either interrogative (istifhāmiyya), in the accusative governed by (yadʿūna), and the second (min) is for specification (li-l-tabyīn). Or it is negative (nāfiya), and (min) is redundant (zāʾida). The word (shayʾ) is the object of (tadʿūna). Or (ma) is verbal-masdar (maṣdariyya) in the sense of the invocation, and (shayʾ) is a masdar with the same meaning. Or it is a relative (mawṣūla), the object of (yaʿlama), and the object of (yadʿūna) is its omitted returning pronoun. The statement, on the first two readings, is an expression of their ignorance and an emphasis of the parable; on the last, it is a warning to them. This was stated by al-Qadi. ﴿And He is the Mighty, the Wise﴾ [al-ʿAnkabut: 42].

﴿And these parables﴾ [al-ʿAnkabut: 43], meaning this parable and its like in the Revelation, ﴿We present to the people﴾ [al-ʿAnkabut: 43], meaning: so that what is remote from their understanding may be brought near. It is narrated from ʿAmr ibn Murra who said: "I never passed by a verse of the Book of Allah that I did not recognise, except that it saddened me, because I heard Allah, Exalted is He, say: ﴿And these parables We present to the people, but none understands them except the learned﴾ [al-ʿAnkabut: 43]."

﴿Allah created the heavens and the earth in truth﴾ [al-ʿAnkabut: 44], meaning: rightly, observing wisdoms and interests, exalted above creating them for any vanity. The bāʾ here is of accompaniment (li-l-mulābasa), and the prepositional phrase is a circumstantial clause (ḥāl). (p-4752) The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 29, verses 57–61:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[57–61] ﴿Every soul shall taste death; then to Us you will be returned.﴾ ﴿And those who believe and do righteous deeds – We will surely settle them in lofty chambers in Paradise, beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. How excellent is the reward of the workers.﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 58] ﴿Those who are patient and upon their Lord rely.﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 59] ﴿And how many a creature there is that carries not its provision; Allah provides for it and for you. Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 29, verses 68–69:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[68–69] ﴿And who is more unjust than one who invents a lie against Allah or denies the truth when it has come to him? Is there not in Hell a residence for the disbelievers?﴾ ﴿And those who strive for Us, We will surely guide them to Our ways. And indeed, Allah is with the doers of good.﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 69]

﴿And who is more unjust than one who invents a lie against Allah﴾ by claiming that He has a partner. ﴿Or denies the truth when it has come to him﴾, meaning the Messenger or the Book. ﴿Is there not in Hell a residence for the disbelievers?﴾ i.e., a place of dwelling, as a recompense for their fabrication and their disbelief. Indeed: ﴿And those who strive for Us﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 69], i.e., strive against the self (nafs), the Satan, the (base) desire (hawa), and the enemies of the religion, for Our sake and seeking Our countenance: ﴿We will surely guide them to Our ways﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 69], i.e., the paths of journeying toward Us and arriving at Our presence. And that is through acts of obedience and striving: ﴿And indeed, Allah is with the doers of good﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 69], i.e., He is with their deeds by way of victory and assistance.
